title: No English word for 아까워 😭 (too good to waste) #learnkorean
caption:
아까워 (a-kka-wo) = "too good to waste" 😭
English has no single word for it — and Mongle will NOT let that last spoonful go.

You can say 아까워 when:
🍚 food is left on the plate
⏰ your time gets wasted
💸 money goes on something useless

Words in this video:
다 드셨죠~? (da deu-syeot-jyo~?) = All done? (polite)
아까워! (a-kka-wo!) = Too good to waste!
더 줄게~ (deo jul-ge~) = I'll give you more~

Tip: 아까워 is casual. With someone older or a stranger, say 아까워요 (a-kka-wo-yo).

pinnedComment: What's too good to waste for YOU? 👇
alt: A needle-felt miniature Korean snack-bar table in warm light. A felt shop lady in a red headscarf and mustard apron reaches for an iron tray with one last spoonful of fried rice and asks 다 드셨죠~? (All done?). Mongle, a coral felt blob mascot with no arms, leaps up and clings to the edge of the lifted tray with its chin, crying 아까워! (Too good to waste!). The lady freezes, then bursts out laughing. A card explains: 아까워 (a-kka-wo) = too good to waste — no single English word. She sets the tray back down, heaps it full of fried rice and says 더 줄게~ (I'll give you more~), and star-eyed Mongle hugs the full tray.
